findings.title: Empty schema matcher does not protect preprocessing input uncertainty
findings.reason: A meaningful mutation narrowing the preprocess input projection from unknown to string survives the individual test. Assert the email schema itself equals an unrestricted schema, and check a representative non-string input accepted after preprocessing; the current nested empty-object partial matcher accepts arbitrary added constraints.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: The test fixture at lines 93–96 actually reaches the preprocess branch with z.preprocess(value => String(value), z.string()). The mutant replaces return z.unknown() with return z.string() at scripts/ci/admin-contract-schemas.ts:143, so the input projection now adds type: string and rejects non-string inputs that preprocessing can convert successfully. The baseline and mutant each ran exactly this one test and both passed. This is not equivalent and not an unexecuted branch: that fixture contains the preprocess expression, the source-only evaluator returns the mutated schema for its email field, and z.toJSONSchema projects that schema. The line-98 toMatchObject expectation contains email: {}, which accepts any extra properties on email, including the incorrect type restriction. Therefore the assertion does not enforce the preprocessing uncertainty named by the test.

findings.title: Schema discovery assertions require an undocumented array order
findings.reason: Line 97 requires limitation paths in the exact order [$.name, $.email], and line 110 requires schema locations in the exact order [path, body]. The locked intake, ADR 0028 and RequestSchemasResult interface require complete deterministic output but specify neither of these source-traversal orders. Another deterministic traversal can preserve the behavior while failing these tests. Compare normalized sets or sorted arrays, or use unordered membership plus exact cardinality; retain direct assertions for each schema and body classification.
